title: Square matrix multiplication: arithmetic exponent over a field

model.instance: All $A,B\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$ are explicit inputs, with field F fixed in advance.

assumptions.description: All input entries may be read; there is no black-box matrix-vector restriction.

model.parameter_domain_description: Require n ≥ 1 and n → ∞, with F fixed in advance.
model.description_zh: The parameter $A,B\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$ is arbitrary; the domain $\mathbb F$ is fixed in advance, and matrix order is $n\to\infty$.
description_paragraphs: The quantity $A,B\in\mathbb{F}^{n\times n}$ is arbitrary. The field $\mathbb{F}$ is fixed in advance, and the matrix order is $n\to\infty$.

operations.query_signature: Read the complete explicit pair (A,B) or access its field elements by index.
operations.response_signature: Exact elements of the input domain; the product $AB$ is not returned directly.
operations.order_convention: Native matrix access; no scalar derivative order is assigned.
operations.coupling: The same fixed explicit input may be reread. Reading does not add multiplication capability.
operations.index_control: Input entries are accessed by address; there is no matrix-vector probing schedule.

oracle.query_domain_description: All entries of $A,B$ are explicit inputs; input access does not make matrix multiplication free.
oracle.description_zh: All input entries are supplied as exact field elements, with no hidden-matrix query interface. Addition, subtraction, and multiplication over the public field have unit arithmetic cost; associated preprocessing cannot be hidden for free.
description_paragraphs: All input entries are supplied as exact field elements, with no hidden-matrix query interface. Addition, subtraction, and multiplication over the public field have unit arithmetic cost; associated preprocessing cannot be hidden for free.

output.allowed_postprocessing: Return every entry of AB and count all arithmetic producing it. Computing the full product is not free postprocessing.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.
output.description_zh: Return every entry of the product $C$ exactly for all inputs.

metric.finiteness_conditions: Every admissible compatible input has a unique matrix product.
metric.goal_latex: \widehat C=AB\quad\text{for all inputs},\qquad \omega_{\mathbb F}=\inf\{\tau:\text{ exact multiplication uses }O(n^\tau)\text{ field operations}\}
metric.description_zh: The base loss is $\mathbf1\{\widehat C\ne AB\}$ and must always vanish. Native complexity is the infimum exponent of exact arithmetic work.
description_paragraphs: The base loss is $\mathbf1\{\widehat C\ne AB\}$ and must always be zero. Native complexity is the infimum exponent of exact arithmetic work.

bracket.envelope_certificate: The bound $\omega_F\le9/4$ does not establish an endpoint running time $O(n^{9/4})$. It implies $O_\zeta(n^{9/4+\zeta})$ for every $\zeta>0$. An exponent gap is not an unqualified complexity ratio $n^{1/4}$.

proofs.title: Matrix-multiplication tensor flattening and dimension lower bounds
proofs.body: The matrix-multiplication tensor has flattening rank n^2 in each input/output mode. The rank of a flattening is a lower bound on tensor rank. Standard bilinearization of an exact arithmetic circuit incurs only a constant factor in operation count, so the arithmetic exponent is at least 2.
